title: Making a tool that lets you vibe-create games
author: lukeiamyourpapi
selftext: Hey everyone! I'm making a tool that lets you create games without any prior game dev experience. It's still early, if anyone is interested in providing feedback, I'd be happy to give lifetime free access when it is out. Your feedback will directly shape the product. Anyone interested?

replies.author: kytheon
replies.body:
Two things.

People don't always play the game that's the most fun. They'll play the game that has them hooked, and that can be a very unfun addictive non-game.

  
And we were talking about an AI that players can use to design their own games. Players on average are not game designers, so they're not going to design fun games. It'll be simplistic and repetitive.

"Won't they play the most fun...?"

The point is that they play **their own game** instead of what is most fun.

replies.author: EtherealDimension
replies.body:
And now that the average gamer has the ability to create their own game, don't you think thered be a system for sharing the games you made with others? If i brainstorm a new game and overnight have a working FPS game and I genuinely enjoy it, wouldnt I want others to play it? 

There would be youtubers and game devs that now have the ability to make a full fleshed game in a short amount of time, and the people with the best skill and creativity with the AI will be able to create the best game. As always, there will be different genres of games. Some people will play the slop clicking games with no content, but others are looking for a good single player story or a innovative FPS, which would now be easier to make.

comments.author: ProjectFadeTouched
comments.body:
AI has no business in the artistic space, and letting it into the door creates an unstable future for any artist. 

This is a bad idea. I'm sorry, OP, but it's just not the move. 

Video games especially are not something that should be coming from a machine, even if "prompted" by a person. Part of the reason we love these things so much is because of the human element in them, the soul. You tale that away and it's not the same.
